title: Sales Enablement: Go-to-Market Complete Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference GTM motions (self-serve, mid-market, and enterprise). It consolidates positioning & messaging, competitive briefs, a pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ to support AEs, SEs, and channel partners.

Audience: Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Solutions Architects, SDRs, Growth Marketing, and GTM leadership.

Contents (quick links)
1. Positioning & Messaging
2. Competitive Briefs (top competitors)
3. Pitch Deck / Demo Narrative
4. Pricing Guidance & Packaging Rules of Thumb
5. Case Study: Marketplace SaaS (example)
6. Security & Compliance FAQ for Prospects
7. SE Technical Checklist and Sales Assets
8. Next steps & owners

---

1) Positioning & Messaging

Executive 30-second pitch: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, production-grade LLM serving across hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. We help engineering teams reduce inference unit cost, control latency, and maintain reliability and compliance without building a custom serving stack.

Core value props (3 pillars)
- Predictable performance: SLA-ready runtime with per-route latency SLOs, telemetry for latency and cost, and deterministic autoscaling for Dedicated customers.
- Cost-to-quality optimization: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations and model routing to minimize per-token cost without sacrificing output quality.
- Deployment flexibility & compliance: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) with enterprise controls (KMS/HSM, audit logs, VPC peering).

Target personas and messaging hooks
- Platform/Infrastructure (engineer): Emphasize deployment options (Dedicated, Private), deterministic capacity planning, and control plane integrations (Terraform module + IaC templates).
- Product/ML engineer: Emphasize dev experience (SDKs, streaming responses, function/tool calls), model catalog, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals.
- Security/Compliance officer: Emphasize audit logging, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, SOC2 compliance, and contractual data residency.
- GTM/Business buyer: Emphasize unit economics, predictable cost, and time-to-market advantages versus building in-house.

Proof points / evidence lines (use in talks and collateral)
- Benchmarks: <20 ms p50 token latency for typical 8k-context completions on Redwood Dedicated (GPU type) - see benchmarking page (link in related_pages).
- Cost reduction: Customers report 25-60% lower inference unit cost after adopting caching + batching recommendations.
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime SLA option for Dedicated customers; hosted API SLA references.

Messaging traps to avoid
- Don't pitch Redwood as just another model provider. The differentiator is serving (runtime + ops + rollout tooling).
- Don't overpromise model accuracy; align on eval-driven quality monitoring and regression guardrails.

---

2) Competitive Briefs (top competitor comparisons)

Competitive frame: Compare along three axes - Performance (latency, throughput), Economics (per-token/unit cost + reserved pricing), and Operational Controls (privacy, VPC, SLAs, observability).

Competitors to call out (short briefs)
- Major cloud provider managed endpoints (e.g., CloudAI Endpoints)
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, global regions, broad compliance portfolio.
  - Weaknesses: higher unit cost at scale, less opinionated inference optimizations, slower iteration on batching/quantization tooling.
  - Win strategy: emphasize Redwood's better unit economics and runtime optimizations, unified API across private/dedicated/hosted.
- LLM API provider A (model-first provider)
  - Strengths: simple API and generous model catalog.
  - Weaknesses: limited enterprise deploy options and weaker control over inference economics.
  - Win strategy: highlight Dedicated and Private options, and deployment parity for enterprise workloads.
- Self-hosted inference frameworks (open-source runtimes)
  - Strengths: price control, full on-prem ownership.
  - Weaknesses: operational burden, slower iteration, lack of service-level guarantees.
  - Win strategy: communicate total cost of ownership, engineering time saved, and Redwood's on-prem packaging & day-2 ops support.

Competitive battle card (talking points)
- If customer cares about latency: surface per-model perf profiles, p50/p95 numbers, and offer benchmark run for customer workload.
- If customer cares about cost: quantify expected savings using their request distribution (offer modeling workbook).
- If customer cares about compliance: position Private deployment + KMS + audit logging + SOC2 as first-class.

---

3) Pitch Deck / Demo Narrative (10-12 slides recommended)

Slide-by-slide outline (one-line notes for presenter)
1. Title & intro: Redwood Inference + tagline - mission in one sentence.
2. Problem: Inference at scale is unpredictable - cost, latency, and ops are painful.
3. Our approach: Runtime + orchestration + dev UX (unified API across environments).
4. Product overview: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private - quick bullets on when to choose each.
5. Architecture diagram: show serving runtime, routing, caching, and control plane.
6. Performance & cost benchmarks: p50/p95 and cost comparisons versus cloud managed and DIY.
7. Enterprise controls: security, VPC, KMS, audit logs, compliance certifications.
8. Customer stories: two short case studies with metrics (reduced latency, cost savings).
9. Pricing & packaging: high-level tiers and reserved capacity examples.
10. Rollout plan: pilot -> canary -> full rollout + support and SRE onboarding.
11. Demo / live walkthrough: quick API call and dashboard view (observability).
12. Ask & next steps: POC offer, technical checklist, proposed timeline.

Demo script tips for SEs
- Show a single API request streaming response, then show cost breakdown and token-level trace.
- Run a small benchmark on the customer's model / prompt set (if available) and show quantization tradeoffs.
- Walk through rollback/fallback behavior (switching to a cheaper model variant on overload).

Assets to attach to deck
- Benchmark PDFs, model performance profiles, sample Terraform module snippet, pricing calculator link.

---

4) Pricing Guidance & Packaging Rules of Thumb

High-level pricing tiers (illustrative; reference official pricing doc for exact numbers):
- Hosted API (self-serve): usage-based pricing (per-token for generation, per-request for embeddings). Free tier credits for quick tests.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual reserved GPU pools + usage overage rules. Predictable throughput, SLA-backed.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): licensing fee (annual) + support tier + optional Dedicated-like reserved capacity.

Packaging and negotiation playbook
- Early-stage customers (< $1k/mo): promote Hosted API and quickstart templates. Offer 30-60 days of free credits and onboarding playbook.
- Scaling customers ($1k- $50k/mo): propose Dedicated pilot (1-3 months) with a conversion path to reserved capacity commit. Include a POC success criteria doc.
- Enterprise (> $50k/mo or regulated workloads): propose Private deployment or Dedicated with strict network isolation and annual commitment. Include SOC2 contractual terms and extended support.

Discounting guidelines (SECs + AMs)
- Avoid discounting list price for Hosted API under $10k ARR - use credits, extended terms or added services.
- For Dedicated, offer graduated discounts tied to commit size and multi-year terms.
- Always include deployment/enablement SOW for Private and Dedicated deals (day-2 ops + training).

Commercial metrics to bring to deals
- Estimated monthly inference unit cost vs current baseline (show modeled % savings).
- Expected latency improvements (p50/p95) and SLO targets.
- Time to value (days to production) and engineering hours saved.

---

5) Case Study (Representative example)

Customer: Acme Marketplace (SaaS, mid-market)
Challenge: Heavy usage of product recommendations via LLMs resulted in high per-token spend and unpredictable latency during peak traffic.
Solution: Redwood onboarded Acme onto Dedicated with model routing and prefix caching. We ran a char-based prompt optimization and recommended INT8 quantization for a compatible model.
Outcomes (90-day results)
- Cost: 38% reduction in per-request inference unit cost.
- Latency: p95 latency reduced from 740ms to 180ms for 512-token completions.
- Reliability: Achieved 99.95% availability on Dedicated SLA after autoscaling policy tuning.
Customer quote: "Redwood let us move from sporadic outages and runaway inference cost to a predictable, performant system without hiring a dedicated infra team."

Playbook to reproduce (for SEs)
1. Collect sample traffic distribution and prompts (2 weeks).
2. Run benchmark on candidate models and quantization profiles (1 week).
3. Deploy Dedicated pilot with caching and autoscaling policies (2-4 weeks).
4. Measure metrics, tune batcher and cache TTLs, then propose reserved commit.

---

6) Security & Compliance FAQ for Prospects (top questions & answers)

Q: How do you handle customer data in the hosted API?
A: Customer payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3) and at rest. We do not use customer data to train models. For regulated customers who require stronger guarantees, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments which provide data isolation and optional customer-managed KMS.

Q: What certifications and audits do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls; audit evidence summaries are available under NDA. We also provide penetration test reports and third-party attestations on request.

Q: Can we run Redwood entirely inside our VPC / air-gapped on-prem?
A: Yes. Private deployments support VPC-hosted control planes and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. We provide an onprem packaging checklist, day-2 ops runbook, and assisted installation option.

Q: How is key management handled?
A: Customers can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring their own keys via integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM providers. Customer-managed keys are supported for encryption-at-rest of model artifacts and logs.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs include request metadata (timestamps, route, model version, token counts) and operator actions (deploy, rollback, policy changes). Logs can be forwarded to the customer's SIEM via secure forwarding and stored with configurable retention policies.

Q: Do you retain prompts or outputs?
A: Default retention for request payloads is 30 days for troubleshooting, configurable by enterprise customers. Dedicated/Private deployments can set retention to customer policy or disable retention; we also offer an option to redact PII automatically via pre-ingest filters.

Q: What data residency controls exist?
A: Hosted regions are selectable; for strict residency needs we recommend Private deployments or Dedicated capacity in a specified region. We provide contractual assurances for data residency in enterprise contracts.

Q: What SLAs and incident response processes are available?
A: We offer a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated customers (higher tiers available), with SLO dashboards exposed in Redwood Console. Incident response includes 24/7 paging for enterprise support plans and a documented incident response runbook.

Security negotiation tips for AEs/SEs
- Capture the customer's minimum security bar early in discovery and map each requirement to a product capability (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Use the security checklist (below) as a pre-sales gating artifact.

Security pre-sales checklist (for SEs to confirm before POC)
- Required compliance certifications (SOC2/ISO/etc.)
- Network topology: VPC peering, private endpoints, firewall rules
- KMS/secret management choices and key ownership model
- Data retention and redaction policy
- Required logging destinations and retention periods
- Incident escalation contacts and required SLAs

---

7) SE Technical Checklist & Sales Assets (what to hand to customer)

Pre-POC pack to send (attach these to any enterprise outreach)
- Architecture diagram (customer-specific), network config example, sample Terraform module.
- Benchmark workbook (Excel/CSV): request distribution, latency/cost model, recommended config.
- SOW template for pilot (includes enablement, runbook handoff, 2-week performance tuning).
- Security package: SOC2 summary, encryption whitepaper, KMS integration guide.

Field play tips for SEs
- Offer a 2-4 week Dedicated pilot with success criteria tied to cost and latency improvement.
- Perform an initial 1-hour workshop for engineering stakeholders to collect traffic and constraints.
- Use the benchmark workbook to set realistic expectations and quantify savings.

Objection handling quick phrases
- "We can't accept vendor-managed models" -> "We support model version pinning and Private deployments so you control the model artifacts and can run in your environment."
- "We have strict retention rules" -> "We can deploy Dedicated with customer-managed retention and redaction filters; we'll capture this in the SOW."

---

8) Next steps & owners

Standard GTM play options
- Quick PoC (Hosted): 2-7 days to stand up test harness and sample prompts using Hosted API. Owner: SDR/AE.
- Dedicated Pilot: 2-4 weeks pilot with tuned batching, caching, and autoscaling. Owner: AE + SE + Solutions Architect.
- Private onboarding: project plan (4-12 weeks) including network setup, KMS integration, and day-2 ops. Owner: Solutions Engineering + Customer Success + Eng Private Deployments.
